title: Kitchen Remodeling Software: 6 Tools for Design, Selections, Leads
html:
Kitchen remodeling software works best as a short chain: a design tool, a selections and budget tool, and a lead tool. SketchUp draws the layout, JobTread tracks selections and change orders, and HubSpot or Calendly catch the consultation request. Published plans run from free to $199 a month before extra users.

Kitchen remodeling software has to survive the longest decision cycle in home services. A kitchen buyer compares layouts, picks cabinets and counters, and changes a choice three times before demo day. This guide sorts six tools by the step they handle, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit.

The expensive mistakes in a kitchen job are rarely framing mistakes. They are a backsplash that was never priced, an appliance that arrived in the wrong size, or a lead who asked for a consultation and got no reply for two days. Each tool below targets one of those gaps.

Which tools catch kitchen remodeling leads and consultations?

HubSpot CRM and Calendly are the cheapest way to log a kitchen lead and book the first visit. A kitchen buyer often contacts three firms, so the first fast reply matters.

  • HubSpot CRM: a contact and deal tracker. The Free plan covers up to 2 users and 1,000 contacts with no time limit, and Starter has a $20 per seat list price, with a new customer discount of $10 per seat month to month. Limit: Free email sends are capped at 2,000 a month and carry HubSpot branding.
  • Calendly: lets a homeowner pick a time for a design consultation. Free has one event type and one calendar connection, and Standard is listed at $10 per seat a month. Limit: it books a time but holds no deal history.

Add three fields to every kitchen lead: budget range, timeline and whether the homeowner owns the home. A lead with a clear budget and a six month timeline is a different call from a lead who is browsing. Sort the first group to the top of your list each morning.

A booking link also helps after hours. Put it in your reply to every web inquiry so a homeowner can choose a slot without waiting for a call. Test it on a phone, because most kitchen leads first see it there.

Which kitchen design software helps a remodeler sell the layout?

SketchUp is the design tool in this guide, and it is a sketching tool, not a quoting tool. It helps a homeowner see a layout, and it should never replace a priced estimate.

  • SketchUp: a 3D modeling tool with plans billed per user, annually. Go is $10.75 a month, Pro is $33.25 and Studio is $71.58, and prices exclude tax. Go includes premade furnishings and materials and runs on iPad and web only, and Pro adds the desktop modeler and LayOut 2D documentation. Limit: the page lists no general free plan, and it takes time to learn.

Use a model to settle layout questions early: where the range goes, how far the island sits from the counters and whether a door swings into a path. Then price the layout in your estimate tool. A render that shows an upgrade the budget cannot afford creates a hard conversation later.

Learning cost is real. Plan a few evenings for the first model, and build a small library of your standard cabinet runs. A remodeler who reuses a ten-foot base run and a standard island saves hours on every job after the first.

Which software tracks kitchen selections, budgets and change orders?

JobTread is built around the project, which suits a kitchen where selections drive the cost. It is the main paid project tool in this guide.

  • JobTread: its site describes budget templates, onscreen takeoff, supplier pricing, proposals with e-signatures and selections with good, better and best options and photos. It lists one plan at $199 a month with one user included, and $20 a month for each extra internal user from the second to the tenth. Limit: no free trial is listed, and the annual base price is not shown.

Selections are the heart of a kitchen. Cabinets, counters, tile, fixtures and appliances can each change the price by thousands. Give every selection a due date, an allowance and a name for who approves it. A selection that is late holds up the order, and a delayed order holds up the crew.

Change orders follow the same rule. No extra work starts until the customer has approved a written price. JobTread says customers can accept, deny or request changes in a portal, and that approval record is what protects you at final payment.

ToolJob it doesPublished priceReal limit
HubSpot CRMLead list and dealsFree for 2 usersEmail capped, branded
CalendlyConsultation bookingFree, then $10 a seatOne event type on Free
SketchUpLayout design$10.75 to $71.58 a monthGo is iPad and web only
JobTreadSelections, budgets, jobs$199 a month, 1 userNo free trial listed
QuickBooksAccounting$38 to $140 a monthPromo ends after 3 months
Google Business ProfileLocal listingFree to createNeeds steady upkeep

Prices checked on each vendor page in November 2026. Annual prices are per month billed yearly.

Which tools handle accounting and the local listing for a kitchen remodeler?

QuickBooks handles the books and Google Business Profile handles the local listing. One keeps the money straight and the other keeps the phone ringing.

  • QuickBooks: invoicing, bank feeds and reports. Simple Start is $38 a month, Essentials is $85 and Plus is $140, with promotional prices for the first three months. Limit: the free tier allows 2 invoices a month and 1 bank connection.
  • Google Business Profile: shows your showroom or service area, photos and reviews in Google Search and Maps. Google states that creating a profile and listing your business is free. Limit: it needs steady photos and review replies to stand out.

Finished kitchens are the best content you have. Post photos of every completed job to your profile, with the style and city in the caption.

What does one kitchen remodel look like in software?

One kitchen touches every tool in the chain. Walk a single job through it before you pay for anything.

  • Inquiry: the homeowner finds your listing or site and requests a consultation through a booking link.
  • Consultation: you measure, ask about budget and timeline, and log the answers in the lead record.
  • Layout: a rough model shows two layout options, each tied to an allowance.
  • Proposal: the priced estimate lists allowances for cabinets, counters, tile and appliances, and the customer signs.
  • Selections: each choice gets a due date, and any change above the allowance becomes a change order.
  • Completion: a final invoice goes out, and a review request goes with it while the customer is happy.

If any step lives on a sticky note, it is a place to lose money. Fix the weakest step first instead of buying the whole chain at once.

What does a kitchen remodeling software stack cost?

A small kitchen remodeler can start at about $38 a month and reach about $250 a month. The ranges below use only published prices.

  • Lean: HubSpot Free, Calendly Free and QuickBooks Simple Start at $38 a month. Cost: $38 a month plus card fees.
  • With design: the lean stack plus SketchUp Go at $10.75 a month or Pro at $33.25. Cost: about $49 to $72 a month.
  • Project-based: JobTread at $199 a month with one user, plus QuickBooks Simple Start at $38. Cost: $237 a month, with $20 for each extra internal user.

Compare each total with the profit on one average kitchen. A tool that prevents a single unpriced change order a quarter usually pays for itself. A tool nobody opens does not.

How should a kitchen remodeler manage selections without delays?

Treat selections as a schedule, not a shopping trip. Late choices cause most kitchen delays, and software only helps if the process behind it is clear.

  • Set allowances in the proposal: give a dollar allowance for cabinets, counters, tile, fixtures and appliances, so the customer knows the limit before shopping.
  • Date every choice: work backward from demo day and give each selection a due date based on lead time.
  • Confirm sizes before ordering: appliance and sink specs decide the cabinet cutouts, so approve those first.
  • Record each change: any choice above the allowance becomes a written change order with a price and a signature.
  • Review weekly: a ten minute call with the homeowner each week catches a late selection before it stops the crew.

Ask every vendor how its tool shows the customer what is still open. A simple status list, such as chosen, ordered and delivered, saves a dozen phone calls on a typical kitchen. If the tool cannot show that to the customer, keep a shared sheet beside it.

What mistakes do kitchen remodelers make with software?

Most regrets come from buying for a bigger company than you run. Four mistakes are common.

  • Buying design software first: a render does not fix slow replies or unpriced changes. Start with leads and proposals.
  • Skipping a pilot job: a demo kitchen hides the awkward steps. Run one real job through the tool before committing.
  • No owner: pick one person to enter selections and approvals. If everyone shares the job, nobody does it.
  • Ignoring the customer view: homeowners judge you by how clear the portal and the messages are, so open it as a customer would.

Training is part of the price. Give yourself a week to load templates and test the booking link on a phone. A tool that is half set up creates more mess than a clean spreadsheet.

How do you choose kitchen remodeling software?

Choose kitchen remodeling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it hold allowances and selections, and does it keep a signed record of every change?

Cost: add the plan, extra users and add-ons, then compare against the profit on one average kitchen.

Setup effort: can you load three of your standard cabinet and counter packages in a weekend?

A one-crew remodeler fits the lean stack. A company with several kitchens in progress at once fits a project tool such as JobTread. Pilot one live kitchen before you move every job.

What software does a kitchen remodeler need?

A kitchen remodeler needs a lead tracker, a way to price and sign proposals, and a tool to manage selections and change orders. Add a design tool if you sell layouts. Start with the stage that loses you the most money and add the rest later.

How much does kitchen remodeling software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from free for HubSpot CRM and Calendly to $199 a month for JobTread, with SketchUp from $10.75 a month billed annually. Extra users, card fees and add-ons cost more. A small stack can run from $38 to about $250 a month.

Is SketchUp good for kitchen design?

It is a capable 3D modeling tool for layouts, and Pro adds the desktop modeler and LayOut documentation. It takes time to learn, and the page lists no general free plan. Use it for layout questions, then price the job in a separate estimate tool.

Is there free software for a kitchen remodeling business?

Yes, for leads and booking. HubSpot lists a Free plan for up to 2 users with 1,000 contacts, and Calendly has a Free plan with one event type. Free tools cap email, event types or users, so check the limits before relying on them.

How do kitchen remodelers track selections?

Give every selection an allowance, a due date and an approver, and record each change as a signed change order. A project tool such as JobTread keeps selections beside the budget. Without a tool, a shared sheet works if one person owns it.

How do kitchen remodelers get more consultation requests?

Most requests come from local search, a clear website and reviews. Complete your Google Business Profile, post finished kitchens, and add a booking link to every reply. Search ads can fill gaps once your crew can handle more consultations, so add them second.

Ask every vendor how its tool shows the customer what is still open. A simple status list, such as chosen, ordered and delivered, saves a dozen phone calls on a typical kitchen. If the tool cannot show that to the customer, keep a shared sheet beside it.
##
What mistakes do kitchen remodelers make with software?
Most regrets come from buying for a bigger company than you run. Four mistakes are common.
-
Buying design software first:
a render does not fix slow replies or unpriced changes. Start with leads and proposals.
-
Skipping a pilot job:
a demo kitchen hides the awkward steps. Run one real job through the tool before committing.
-
No owner:
pick one person to enter selections and approvals. If everyone shares the job, nobody does it.
-
Ignoring the customer view:
homeowners judge you by how clear the portal and the messages are, so open it as a customer would.
Training is part of the price. Give yourself a week to load templates and test the booking link on a phone. A tool that is half set up creates more mess than a clean spreadsheet.
##
How do you choose kitchen remodeling software?
Choose kitchen remodeling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.
Fit:
does it hold allowances and selections, and does it keep a signed record of every change?
Cost:
add the plan, extra users and add-ons, then compare against the profit on one average kitchen.
Setup effort:
can you load three of your standard cabinet and counter packages in a weekend?
A one-crew remodeler fits the lean stack. A company with several kitchens in progress at once fits a project tool such as JobTread. Pilot one live kitchen before you move every job.
###
What software does a kitchen remodeler need?
A kitchen remodeler needs a lead tracker, a way to price and sign proposals, and a tool to manage selections and change orders. Add a design tool if you sell layouts. Start with the stage that loses you the most money and add the rest later.
###
How much does kitchen remodeling software cost?
Published prices in this guide run from free for HubSpot CRM and Calendly to $199 a month for JobTread, with SketchUp from $10.75 a month billed annually. Extra users, card fees and add-ons cost more. A small stack can run from $38 to about $250 a month.
###
Is SketchUp good for kitchen design?
It is a capable 3D modeling tool for layouts, and Pro adds the desktop modeler and LayOut documentation. It takes time to learn, and the page lists no general free plan. Use it for layout questions, then price the job in a separate estimate tool.
###
Is there free software for a kitchen remodeling business?
Yes, for leads and booking. HubSpot lists a Free plan for up to 2 users with 1,000 contacts, and Calendly has a Free plan with one event type. Free tools cap email, event types or users, so check the limits before relying on them.
###
How do kitchen remodelers track selections?
Give every selection an allowance, a due date and an approver, and record each change as a signed change order. A project tool such as JobTread keeps selections beside the budget. Without a tool, a shared sheet works if one person owns it.
###
How do kitchen remodelers get more consultation requests?
Most requests come from local search, a clear website and reviews. Complete your Google Business Profile, post finished kitchens, and add a booking link to every reply. Search ads can fill gaps once your crew can handle more consultations, so add them second.
